feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV with a clear senior digital communications profile and logical career progression within one organization. It reads professionally and shows scope, but impact would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience consistently support a senior digital strategy/communications leadership brand.  
- Credibility and progression: promotions within NACo show trust, growth, and increasing responsibility.  
- Relevant detail: strong mix of strategy, platforms, analytics, governance, and multimedia gives a well-rounded leadership profile.

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than outcomes. Include measurable improvements in engagement, efficiency, conversion, adoption, or campaign performance.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating would improve structure and save space.  
- Fix writing/style consistency: use “12 years of experience” (missing “of”); standardize serial commas (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs versions without final comma); “front-end” is fine, but keep hyphenation consistent; “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly—use “French (A2, currently learning)” or similar. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV’s direction, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and adding more role-specific focus would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, more standard phrasing.
- Lead with current positioning and strongest differentiators: digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications systems for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with a sharper value statement tied to outcomes and leadership scope.
- Consider rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience building and leading cross-channel programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in web and CMS modernization, content operations, analytics, and the workflows that support complex stakeholder environments. Strong background in advocacy communications, cross-functional coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows/systems” are repeated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” overlaps with multiple NACo role descriptions and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but the section is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening wording and making competencies more distinctive will improve scan value.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, resume-style phrasing and tighten vague terms: “Multi-channel communications,” “Web platform & CMS administration,” “Analytics, reporting & optimization.”
- Replace generic items with higher-value distinctions drawn from recent roles: “Digital governance & transformation,” “Editorial systems & workflow design,” “AI-enabled search & content discovery.”
- Reduce soft-skill phrasing in this section; move “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” out in favor of a harder capability like “Platform modernization” or “Content operations.”
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & platform modernization • Multi-channel communications • Web platform & CMS administration • Editorial systems & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Content operations & governance • Policy & advocacy communications • AI-enabled search & content discovery • Multimedia & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the header.
- Several items repeat Topline Skills almost verbatim; this section should stay broader and more distilled.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with the prior NACo positions and the “Recent Projects” section. Tighten it around consultant-level scope, recent strategic value, and 2–3 concrete outcomes or named initiatives.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper positioning line: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery initiatives.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 impact-focused bullets; e.g., combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one bullet about improving cross-channel communications operations.
- Replace task phrasing (“develop,” “deliver,” “advise”) with outcome-oriented language: “Built Drupal campaign microsites and modular toolkit templates to speed campaign launches and improve member access to resources.”
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/pages supported, launch timelines reduced, toolkit downloads, search relevance gains, stakeholder teams served, or workflow efficiencies.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search,” microsites, and anniversary/campaign storytelling duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level and let projects hold the detail.
- Governance, analytics, and enterprise web improvement also echo the 2022–2024 Director role; emphasize post-tenure consulting scope instead.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget, leading platform modernization and cross-channel communications operations.”
- Make bullets more results-led: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where missing: quantify team size, budget, reporting cadence, production volume, efficiency gains, or engagement improvements from analytics/governance work.
- Combine lower-value bullets for concision: merge governance + analytics into one operational-improvement bullet; keep the studio bullet because it shows distinctive leadership/build capability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; in this entry, focus on enterprise leadership, modernization and infrastructure.
- Video expansion may partially overlap with earlier weekly advocacy video work; frame this here as building institutional production capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing execution-level ownership, channel growth, and systems/process improvements rather than broad leadership language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with: “Managed day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling NACo’s editorial operations and advocacy messaging.”
- Tighten bullets to focus on concrete ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet to show outcome: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine planning/workflow bullets: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led” is overused across adjacent roles; use “managed,” “launched,” “produced,” or “improved” here.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered more strongly in the Director of Digital Media entry.

Suggested edit:

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT” and reads as a tool dump rather than a senior, impact-oriented topline summary. For this section, emphasize platforms and modernization themes most tied to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a list of tools to a concise capability line, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put Drupal first and consider dropping WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages here unless they are important targets; they’re better preserved in “Technical + IT.”
- Replace “Airtable systems” with “Airtable-based content systems” or “Airtable workflow systems” for clearer business value.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector sites” to echo the 10,000+ page migration.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; avoid repeating the same platform names in both places.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies; keep it in only one topline area if space is tight.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit:

- Replace “KPI design” with “KPI framework development” or “measurement strategy” to sound more senior and specific

Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills: Web Platforms & Technical Execution” and “Core Competencies.” This item should either be tightened to a pure tools list or reframed to emphasize platform administration/modernization depth.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Web Platforms & CMS Administration
- Reorder by strongest/recent relevance: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of just names: Drupal (enterprise content architecture, migrations) • WordPress (site administration) • SharePoint / Power Pages (Microsoft ecosystem publishing) • GitHub Pages (lightweight static sites)
- Keep it strictly platform-focused; avoid adding modernization, workflows, APIs, or front-end terms already covered elsewhere

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same platforms plus broader technical capabilities
- “Web & CMS administration” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating generic phrasing without added specificity

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. It should emphasize current, relevant implementation strengths and group tools more cleanly.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite for clarity and hierarchy: “Front-end development: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery • Technical implementation: API integrations, Google Tag Manager • Serverless/automation: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless used elsewhere consistently; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner.
- Put the strongest, most current capabilities first: JavaScript, API integrations, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions.
- If accurate, add scope or use context elsewhere in the CV, e.g., “custom front-end implementation,” “deployment automation,” or “tag management for analytics.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This substantially duplicates Topline Skills [2] (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations”); vary wording or remove repeated terms from one section.
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under Analytics/Optimization than Coding & Technical Implementation.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize capability, e.g. “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems” or “Workflow Design & Project Operations Tools.”
- Group by function to improve scan value: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Team collaboration: Slack, Teams.”
- If space allows, add a light qualifier tied to recent work: “used to build editorial planning, approval workflows, cross-team coordination, and lightweight operational systems.”
- Consider trimming weaker/older tools if not central to recent roles; keep the most relevant to current consulting/director work first: Airtable, Power Automate, Jira, Asana, Slack, Teams.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same language verbatim.
- Slack/Teams may feel generic unless framed as collaboration systems rather than core technical tools.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful category, but it reads as a bare software list and misses the scale/strategic email work shown in recent NACo roles. Strengthen it by signaling CRM/email automation capability without repeating newsletter details already covered in experience.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing, CRM & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Email campaign operations • Audience segmentation • Journey automation**
- If accurate, add one higher-value capability instead of more tools: **list management**, **template deployment**, or **engagement reporting**
- Keep platform names in order of strongest/recent relevance; if Dynamics 365 is most current, leave it first

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid adding “newsletters,” “tens of thousands,” or channel ownership here; those are already covered well in recent NACo experience
- Don’t repeat analytics terms already listed under “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” unless email-specific reporting is a real differentiator

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs or scale if you can quantify them.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and establish workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add measurable scope where possible: website refresh size, number of livestreams/videos produced, newsletter or audience reach, event volume, or team size supported.
- Tighten the second sentence around outcomes: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, expanding in-house production capacity.”
- Replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with a stronger management phrase if accurate: “mentored” or “supervised” a digital media associate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this as launching or piloting the format here.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats language used in later NACo entries; position this as establishing initial processes instead.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/multimedia. Emphasize the podcast launch and frame the rest as support to policy/program priorities.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the clearest achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams; launched the organization’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- Tighten “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” to something more specific, e.g. “produced digital and multimedia content to support member communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add scope or outcome: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or how the podcast/content supported advocacy, member engagement, or organizational visibility.
- Keep this entry to 1–2 lines since later roles show the fuller digital leadership progression.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later NACo entries; avoid repeating generic multimedia language.
- Don’t overstate digital leadership here, since the stronger web/video/team leadership appears in 2015–2024 roles.
